assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and made place, family background, and policy central empirical economic questions.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the research program; Friedman is a major collaborator in its landmark early work.
assessment.maturity: The evidence base, methods, and influence on public and labour economics are extensive and sustained.
uncertainties: The full intellectual contribution extends beyond three researchers, including important contributions by Lawrence F. Katz.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work supplied influential evidence and a durable framework for understanding how technology, trade exposure, and tasks reshape local labour markets and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson form a coherent core for the trade-shock and labour-demand contribution.
assessment.maturity: Its findings have been replicated, extended, and incorporated into broad debates on labour-market adjustment.
uncertainties: Separating the trade-shock contribution from the wider literature on technology and inequality is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research established that early-life health and environments have consequential long-run effects and connected those facts to the economics of human-capital formation.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond, and Cunha represent complementary empirical and conceptual foundations of the listed contribution.
assessment.maturity: A large subsequent literature and diverse quasi-experimental evidence make the contribution mature.
uncertainties: The intellectual boundaries between child health, skill formation, and the broader human-capital literature remain broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The combination of theory and credible empirical measurement reshaped economic analysis of adverse selection and insurance-market design.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav, and Salanie provide a defensible three-person attribution spanning empirical implementation and theoretical foundations.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been widely used across health, insurance, and other contract settings for many years.
uncertainties: Credit for foundational asymmetric-information theory necessarily extends beyond the listed group.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on employer market power has substantially changed how economists interpret wages, labour-market institutions, and policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning is the clearest conceptual anchor; Naidu and Ashenfelter represent important theoretical and empirical strands.
assessment.maturity: The field has accumulated substantial evidence and has major influence on contemporary labour economics.
uncertainties: The candidate label combines distinct theoretical, empirical, and institutional literatures, making a single prize formulation challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence methods produced persuasive evidence on discrimination and changed empirical research on labour-market inequality.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are central to a landmark modern audit study, while Charles is a leading contributor to the broader economics of discrimination.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been extensively applied across settings and has enduring scientific and policy influence.
uncertainties: Attribution is difficult because audit-study methods and discrimination research have many foundational contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods made influential empirical work feasible when persistent outcomes and unobserved heterogeneity complicate identification.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are central to the core estimator, with Blundell central to its major system-GMM extension.
assessment.maturity: These methods have had decades of broad use and methodological scrutiny.
uncertainties: Their very wide application has also exposed sensitivity to instrument proliferation and specification choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research made informal insurance, risk sharing, and household and village institutions empirically tractable in development economics.
assessment.attribution: Townsend, Rosenzweig, and Udry are appropriate central figures for the linked theoretical and field-empirical program.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is longstanding and has shaped research on risk, credit, and development institutions.
uncertainties: Evidence on the extent and mechanisms of risk sharing can be context-specific.
